1: # Markdown and Google Docs Synchronization
2: 
3: Guidelines for importing markdown files, handling LaTeX equations, and resolving
4: sync conflicts.
5: 
6: ## Import Markdown
7: 
8: Use `mutate import-md` to convert any markdown file into a native Google Doc
9: with proper formatting (headings, bold, italic, links, lists, tables):
10: 
11: ```bash
12: "$GDOCS" mutate import-md /path/to/report.md --title "Weekly Report"
13: ```
14: 
15: To update an existing document instead of creating a new one, use the `--update`
16: flag:
17: 
18: ```bash
19: "$GDOCS" mutate import-md /path/to/report.md --update DOC_ID
20: ```
21: 
22: ### Trade-offs: `import-md --update` vs. `sync`
23: 
24: When updating an existing document from a markdown file, choose the tool based
25: on your needs:
26: 
27: *   **Use `mutate import-md --update`** when you want **clean formatting**
28:     (native tables, lists, code blocks).
29:     *   *Warning*: This operation **overwrites the entire document** and
30:         **destroys all existing comments, suggestions, and anchors**.
31: *   **Use `mutate sync`** (see below) when you need to **preserve comments and
32:     collaborate**. It performs a 3-way merge to keep comments intact, but may
33:     occasionally introduce minor formatting artifacts (e.g., literal markdown
34:     characters).
35: 
36: > [!CAUTION] Every `mutate` command applies its changes to the live document
37: > immediately. There is no staged review step and no accept/reject safety net,
38: > so a destructive import cannot be undone from the CLI. Confirm with the user
39: > before overwriting a document that other people are working in, and see
40: > [metadata_retention.md](metadata_retention.md) for the pre-edit checks.
41: 
42: This is the simplest way to turn a local `.md` file into a shareable Google Doc.
43: The doc is created in your Drive root and the URL is printed on success. Combine
44: with `mutate share` to distribute:
45: 
46: ```bash
47: DOC_ID=$("$GDOCS" mutate import-md /tmp/notes.md --title "Notes" --json | jq -r .documentId)
48: "$GDOCS" mutate share $DOC_ID --email team@example.com --role writer
49: ```
50: 
51: ## Hyperlinks in Markdown
52: 
53: When preparing markdown files for Google Docs import (`mutate import-md` or
54: `mutate sync`), format links to source files as web-accessible URLs rather than
55: local filesystem paths:
56: 
57: *   **Restricted `file:///` Usage:** `file:///` links should **ONLY** be used
58:     when the user explicitly requests local filesystem links. Never use
59:     `file:///` as the default protocol for markdown imported into Google Docs.
60: *   **Why:** Google Workspace web applications enforce strict browser security
61:     policies (Same-Origin Policy) that block `file://` URI schemes. If
62:     `file:///` links are imported into a Google Doc, clicking them in a browser
63:     will be blocked by the browser, rendering the links dead.
64: 
65: ## Handling LaTeX Equations & Math Formulas
66: 
67: > [!IMPORTANT] The Google Docs API and Google Drive's native Markdown converter
68: > do NOT parse LaTeX delimiters (`$` / `$$`). Raw LaTeX formulas will survive
69: > the conversion only as literal unparsed text, with mangled underscores (`\_`)
70: > and broken table borders.
71: 
72: Adopt this two-track standard for any document containing math:
73: 
74: 1.  **Inline Math & Table Headers:** Format using native Unicode typography
75:     (`v₁`, `v₂`, `Δv`, `T₀`, `ΔV`, `%`, `→`, `×`, `²`, `±`). Never use `$x$` in
76:     table cells or inline text.
77: 2.  **Block / Display Equations:** Google Docs cannot typeset `$$...$$`,
78:     `\[...\]`, or `\begin{equation}`. Either rewrite the equation with Unicode
79:     typography, or render it to an image yourself and reference the local image
80:     file from the markdown — `import-md` and `sync` upload local images
81:     automatically (see "Automatic Image Uploads in Sync" below).
82: 
83: **Guardrails & validation:** `mutate import-md` and `mutate sync` automatically
84: scan markdown files for unrendered LaTeX math delimiters outside code blocks. If
85: detected:
86: 
87: -   A diagnostic warning is emitted to `stderr` with remediation steps.
88: -   Passing `--strict-math` causes `import-md` to fail immediately, preventing
89:     accidental publication of broken mathematical formatting.
90: 
91: ## Handling Mermaid Diagrams
92: 
93: Drive's native Markdown converter does not turn Mermaid blocks (` ```mermaid `)
94: into images on import, so a Mermaid block passed through `import-md` lands in
95: the document as a literal code block.
96: 
97: See [`diagrams.md`](diagrams.md) for the supported diagram workflows, including
98: pre-rendering a diagram to an image and referencing it from the markdown.
99: 
100: ## Handling Conflicts during Sync
101: 
102: When using `mutate sync` to synchronize a local markdown file with a Google Doc,
103: conflicts may occur if both the local file and the remote doc have changed since
104: the last sync.
105: 
106: By default, `mutate sync` will fail with an error listing the conflicts.
107: 
108: To handle conflicts, you can use the following flags:
109: 
110: *   **`--json-conflicts`**: Outputs conflicts as a JSON string prefixed with
111:     `CONFLICT_JSON:`, which is useful for programmatic parsing.
112: 
113:     ```bash
114:     "$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md --json-conflicts
115:     ```
116: 
117: *   **`--prefer-local`**: Automatically resolves conflicts by keeping the local
118:     changes and filtering out conflicting remote edits.
119: 
120:     ```bash
121:     "$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md --prefer-local
122:     ```
123: 
124: *   **`--local-base`**: Saves the local file content directly as the merge base,
125:     bypassing the translation of the remote Google Doc. This is useful when
126:     initializing sync on an existing document where the local file is known to
127:     be the correct baseline, or after a clean reset to avoid translation
128:     artifacts.
129: 
130:     ```bash
131:     "$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md --local-base
132:     ```
133: 
134: > [!IMPORTANT] **Never suggest overwriting or forcing a sync (by deleting the
135: > base file or using `--prefer-local`) without asking the user first!** If
136: > conflicts occur, you MUST present the differences to the user and ask them how
137: > they want to resolve them: 1. Keep Local changes (overwrites remote, e.g.,
138: > using `--prefer-local`). 2. Keep Remote changes (overwrites local). 3. Go
139: > through the differences together to manually merge. Always preserve the user's
140: > remote changes unless they explicitly tell you to discard them.
141: 
142: ## Force Pushing and Resetting Document State
143: 
144: If you need to force-push local content to a Google Doc and ensure all
145: formatting (headings, lists, etc.) is correctly applied, do NOT use `mutate
146: write`. `mutate write` only writes raw text and bypasses the formatting logic,
147: which can lead to a document full of raw markdown syntax if a subsequent `mutate
148: sync` fails to detect changes.
149: 
150: Instead, follow this procedure to force-push and reset state:
151: 
152: 1.  **Clear the document**: Use `"$GDOCS" mutate write DOC_ID --file
153:     <empty_file> --clear` to make the document empty or nearly empty.
154: 2.  **Delete the base file**: Remove the corresponding `.base.md` file from the
155:     sync state directory (a `gdocs_sync/` directory under your agent's data
156:     directory).
157: 3.  **Run sync**: Run `"$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md`. This will
158:     perform a 2-way sync and push all content as new elements with proper
159:     formatting.
160: 
161: > [!WARNING] Always ask the user for permission before performing a force-push
162: > or deleting base files, as this can overwrite remote changes.
163: 
164: ## Marker-Scoped Synchronization (Body Mode)
165: 
166: You can restrict synchronization to a specific range within the document,
167: protecting the rest (like headers and footers) from being overwritten or
168: modified.
169: 
170: To enable this, pass the `--start-marker` and `--end-marker` options:
171: 
172: ```bash
173: "$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md --start-marker "{{DOCUMENT_BODY}}" --end-marker "{{END_DOCUMENT_BODY}}"
174: ```
175: 
176: *   **Behavior**: Diffs and syncs only the content located strictly between the
177:     two markers in both the remote GDoc and the local file.
178: *   **Safety**: If markers are not found or are found in the wrong order, the
179:     tool will report an error to prevent accidental full sync overwrites of
180:     protected zones.
181: 
182: ## Tab-Scoped Synchronization
183: 
184: You can synchronize a local markdown file to a specific tab inside a Google Doc
185: using the `--tab` option:
186: 
187: ```bash
188: "$GDOCS" mutate sync DOC_ID local_file.md --tab TAB_ID
189: ```
190: 
191: This ensures that the sync operations (merging, inserting, and deleting blocks)
192: only target the specified tab, preventing accidental edits to other tabs.
193: 
194: ## Automatic Image Uploads in Sync
195: 
196: When you run `mutate sync`, the tool automatically parses the local markdown
197: file for local image references (e.g. `![diagram](images/diagram.png)`).
198: 
199: Before performing the sync, it:
200: 
201: 1.  Uploads the images securely to Drive (into a temporary folder or parent
202:     folder).
203: 2.  Replaces the local path references in the markdown content with public Drive
204:     content URIs.
205: 
206: This ensures that images are properly rendered as inline images in the Google
207: Doc without requiring manual uploads first.
208: 
209: > [!IMPORTANT]
210: >
211: > **SVG is not supported.** Image uploads fail on `.svg` with `SVG conversion is
212: > not available; convert the image to PNG or JPEG first`. This applies
213: > everywhere images are uploaded — `mutate sync`, `mutate import-md`, `mutate
214: > insert-image-from-file`, and the `insert-image-from-file` batch operation.
215: > Convert diagrams to PNG before referencing them, and note that some diagram
216: > renderers emit SVG by default. See [diagrams.md](diagrams.md).
217: 
218: ## Code Block Syntax Highlighting in Sync
219: 
220: The `mutate sync` command automatically applies syntax highlighting (token-level
221: coloring and font styles like bold/italic) to fenced code blocks in Google Docs.
222: 
223: Supported language tags include:
224: 
225: *   **C / C++**: `cpp`, `c++`, `c`
226: *   **Protocol Buffers**: `proto`, `prototext`, `protobuf`
227: *   **JSON**: `json`
228: *   **Shell / Bash**: `shell`, `sh`, `bash`
229: *   **Python**: `python`, `py`
230: *   **Go**: `go`, `golang`
231: 
232: ## Diagrams in Sync
233: 
234: The `mutate sync` command also supports automatic rendering of code-based
235: diagrams (Mermaid, DOT, and Sequence Diagrams) found in the local Markdown file.
236: See [diagrams.md](diagrams.md) for more details.
